chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazi', from 'Ali al-Sa'i, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal Musa عليه السلام, who said:

He عليه السلام said: "The extent of our knowledge is in three aspects: past, bygone, and newly occurring. As for the past, it is explained; as for the bygone, it is inscribed; and as for the newly occurring, it is a casting into the hearts and a tapping in the ears. And it is the most excellent of our knowledge, and there is no Prophet after our Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم."

key_terms.حَادِثٍ: that which is newly occurring or present
key_terms.عِلْمِنَا: the knowledge belonging to the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.غَابِرٍ: that which is bygone or transmitted from earlier times
key_terms.قَذْفٌ فِي الْقُلُوبِ: a divinely cast inspiration into the hearts
key_terms.مَاضٍ: that which pertains to past matters
key_terms.نَقْرٌ فِي الْأَسْمَاعِ: a subtle communicated impression in the ears

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the different aspects of the Imams' knowledge while affirming the finality of prophethood?
ai.summary: This hadith describes three aspects of the knowledge of the Imams عليهم السلام: knowledge of the past, the bygone, and newly occurring matters. It presents the newly occurring form as divinely conveyed to the hearts and ears, while affirming that such knowledge does not imply prophethood, since there is no Prophet after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from his uncle Hamza Bin Bazie, from Ali Al Saiy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Our<sup>asws</sup> knowledge reaches upon three aspects – the past, the ancient, and the newly occurring (present). So as for the past, so it is interpreted, and as for the ancient, so it Hymned, and as for the newly occurring (present), so it is cast into the hearts, and reverberated in the ears, and it is the most superior of our<sup>asws</sup> knowledge, and there is no Prophet<sup>as</sup> to come after our<sup>asws</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from his paternal uncle Hamzah ibn Bazi‘ from Ali as-Sa’I from abu al-Hassan, the first, Musa (a.s.) who has said the folloowing.

“The totality of our knowledge is of three aspects. Knowledge of the past, future and that coming into being. The knowledge of the past is that which is interpreted. The knowledg eot he future is that which is written and the knowledge of that which come into being is the kind that is thrown into the hearts and is heard by the ears and this is best aspect of our knowledge and there is no prophet after our Holy Prophet (s.a.).”
